paper_metadata.title: Quantum computing for multidimensional option pricing: End-to-end pipeline

summary: The paper presents a gate-based quantum finance pipeline for multidimensional option pricing using QAE-based QAMC: one marginal-density experiment on AXA and two pricing experiments (a 2-asset spread call on AXA/Michelin and a 3-asset arithmetic basket call on AXA/Credit Agricole/Michelin). The reported quantum advantage is theoretical and simulator-based, with 25 repetitions per experiment, 5 qubits plus ancilla for the AXA marginal case, and 7 qubits plus ancilla for the 2-asset pricing case; no physical QPU results or practical runtime advantage are demonstrated.

experiments.description: Quantum accelerated Monte Carlo (QAMC) estimation of cosine-series coefficients for marginal NIG density recovery, compared against classical Monte Carlo, using AXA as the worked example.

algorithm.variant: Real Quantum Amplitude Estimation (R-QAE) for signed coefficient estimation

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Density samples are loaded into amplitudes via an oracle AX_i; cosine basis functions gamma_k are loaded by controlled rotation W_gamma_k. One ancilla qubit stores the amplitude corresponding to the expectation value.
problem_formulation.objective_function: Estimate cosine coefficients a_k = E[gamma_k(X_i)] for the calibrated marginal density f_i, then reconstruct f_i and F_i via truncated cosine series.

problem_instance.description: Marginal density recovery for the AXA 1-year expiry calibrated NIG distribution.

dataset_specification.preprocessing: Calibrated NIG marginal from European option quotes; density compared against classically computed Riemann quadrature reference.

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Use mid-market call/put quotes; infer discount/forward/dividend curves from put-call parity; calibrate NIG parameters with Tikhonov-regularized constrained least squares; use cosine-series truncation for density estimation.
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Each estimation experiment repeated 25 times; compare average absolute error against a classical Riemann quadrature reference; report 90% confidence intervals.

implementation_details.classical_solver: classical Riemann quadrature / classical Monte Carlo baseline
implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Classical calibration of NIG parameters and classical computation of reference coefficients via Riemann quadrature.
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Average errors and confidence intervals over 25 repetitions.

convergence_data.loss_curve_shape: error decreases approximately as O(1/sqrt(L)) classically and O(1/L) quantumly in the reported convergence plot

results.unit: normalized by spot (10 basis points, around ATM)
normalized by spot (approximate ATM error; reported as around 10 basis points)

speedup_claims.conditions: for amplitude estimation / QAMC coefficient estimation
speedup_claims.caveats: The paper reports the expected O(1/epsilon) vs O(1/epsilon^2) scaling and shows convergence plots on a simulator; no physical hardware results are given.

complexity_analysis.quantum_complexity: O(1/epsilon) query complexity for QAE; for marginal recovery, O(sqrt(b_i-a_i) K_i^2 / epsilon_i log(K_i/rho_i)) queries
complexity_analysis.classical_complexity: O(1/epsilon^2) for classical Monte Carlo; for coefficient estimation, classical sampling scales as O(1/epsilon^2)

advantage_assessment.resources_for_advantage: No physical hardware demonstration; only simulator-based QAE vs CMC comparison with 25 repetitions.
limiting_factors: state preparation/oracle loading overhead not benchmarked on hardware
no end-to-end runtime or resource counts reported

notes: num_qubits inferred from J = 2^5 discrete points and the paper's statement that n = 5 qubits are used for the QAMC method, with one ancilla qubit added for amplitude estimation.
hardware.type inferred as simulator_other because the paper states the experiments were run on a quantum simulator in myQLM and does not name a physical QPU.
circuit_depth not reported explicitly; only qubit counts and query complexity are given.
The paper reports a theoretical quadratic improvement for QAMC/QAE over CMC, but the experiment is simulator-based and does not establish practical hardware advantage.

experiments.description: Quantum accelerated Monte Carlo estimation of the final multidimensional option price for a 2-asset spread call, compared with classical Monte Carlo, using AXA and Michelin.

algorithm.variant: Iterative Quantum Amplitude Estimation (IQAE) for positive payoff estimation

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Joint density is loaded into amplitudes via AX; payoff is loaded by controlled rotation W_h. The spread payoff is evaluated under a Gaussian-copula joint distribution built from calibrated NIG marginals.
problem_formulation.objective_function: Estimate V(T,K)=e^{-rT}E[h(S,K)] for h(S1,S2,K)=max(S1-S2-K,0) with K=0.

problem_instance.description: 2-asset spread call option pricing with AXA and Michelin under a Gaussian copula.
problem_instance.dataset_name: Euronext options data for AXA and Michelin

dataset_specification.preprocessing: Calibrated NIG marginals; Gaussian copula with correlation matrix [[1,-0.25],[-0.25,1]]; marginal densities reconstructed with K=27 cosine terms classically to isolate final-price error.

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Use market quotes to calibrate NIG marginals; infer discount/forward/dividend curves; construct Gaussian copula joint distribution; use classically recovered marginals for the final pricing experiment.
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Each estimation experiment repeated 25 times; compare average absolute error against a classically computed Riemann-sum reference; report 90% confidence intervals.

implementation_details.classical_solver: classical Monte Carlo / classically computed Riemann-sum reference
implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Classical calibration of marginals and construction of the Gaussian copula; classical recovery of marginal densities with K=27 terms to isolate pricing error.
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Average errors and confidence intervals over 25 repetitions.

convergence_data.loss_curve_shape: error decreases approximately as O(1/sqrt(L)) classically and O(1/L) quantumly in the reported convergence plot

results.value: O(N^2 c'_max sqrt(I_max) K_max^2 / epsilon_c log(NK_max/rho_c))

speedup_claims.conditions: for QAE-based pricing of the 2-asset spread option
speedup_claims.caveats: The paper states that QAMC follows the expected O(1/epsilon) scaling and that, for high accuracy below 1e-3, it needs 10-100 fewer samples/queries than CMC.
This is reported qualitatively in the text; exact numeric values are not tabulated.

complexity_analysis.quantum_complexity: O(1/epsilon) query complexity for QAE; for the independent formulation, O(N^2 c'_max sqrt(I_max) K_max^2 / epsilon_c log(NK_max/rho_c)) plus oracle costs

advantage_assessment.resources_for_advantage: Simulator-only spread-option pricing with 2 assets, 7 logical qubits, and 25 repetitions; no hardware scaling evidence.
limiting_factors: copula and marginal loading overhead not quantified

circuit_depth not reported explicitly; only query complexity and qubit counts are given.
